steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a small baking dish with cooking spray; set aside.
Cook bacon strips in a large skillet over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels; leave drippings in the skillet.

Remove stems from mushrooms; chop stems and set caps aside. Heat butter with drippings in the skillet until melted; stir in mushroom stems, onion, and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, until onion caramelizes, 15 to 20 minutes; transfer to a blender.
Add bacon, bread crumbs, blue cheese, and cream cheese to the blender; pulse until combined. Stuff cheese mixture into mushroom caps; place in the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbly and lightly browned, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Blue Bacon Stuffed Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: In this blue bacon-stuffed mushrooms recipe, mushrooms are stuffed with blue cheese, bacon, caramelized onions, and garlic for a delicious appetizer.

review.reviewBody: I made these for my New Year’s Eve party and they were a big hit. They are rich and tasty and very easy to make. I made a few small changes 1) I had precooked bacon on hand, so I used that. In place of the bacon fat, I cooked the onions and mushroom stems in olive oil and butter. 2) I used panko instead of regular breadcrumbs. 3) I don’t have a blender, so I just chopped things very fine, and mixed everything together. Finally, I made the filling the day before, then stuffed the mushrooms early the day of the party and refrigerated until I baked them later in the evening. This seemed to work out just fine, and made prep for the party much easier.

I had doubts about this because of the fat content, but honestly I thought it was pretty good and would make it again. I did use 6 ounces of cream cheese and 6 ounces of a blue cheese/gorgonzola mix and separated the bacon grease/fat from the cooked onion mixture before I added it to the cream cheese/blue cheese mixture and I sprayed my mushroom caps with cooking spray before filling and again after they baked for 15 minutes because I thought they looked dry (I may have overstuffed my disposable broiling pan) and then I baked them for another 5 minutes.

But whether or not that made a difference I don't know because these turned out moist and flavorful as they were being devoured. And they did NOT boil over: everything stayed in place.

Not clear on what a large mushroom is - pretty sure they didn't mean portabella - so the pack I bought had 20 mushrooms in 32 ounces. That was just what I could find that wasn't button mushrooms. 

I also had some filling left over (about 2 ounces) and trust me, it's great on crackers, possibly great baked in a dish and then served with crackers on the side. I will save the stuffing recipe for that at least.

I appreciated another reviewer for mentioning to make the stuffing a day ahead and refrigerating for easier prep. I also did NOT use a blender or mixer. This filling was very stiff and easy to work with after mixing so filling the mushrooms only required rolling it into a ball and pressing it into the mushroom cap. I will save this and m
Only change I made was adding 1/3 cup diced fresh spinach to the saute mix at the end and a lil sea salt and cracked fresh pepper to the mix. I did not put through blender. These are awesome!!!

I used a food processor to to blend the filling mixture together, so I could retain a little texture. Husband is doing keto, so I dropped in a few pork rinds to substitute, since bread crumbs wouldn't do on keto. One note, while the baking times suggested is great for the filling, it leaves the mushrooms very firm, so next time we make it, we might grill or otherwise lightly pre-cook the mushroom caps, prior to filling them before baking.

They went so fast my husband complained that he only got two at our party. The only changes I made was to mix by hand and not in the blender the ingredients. I also added chopped fresh parsley for color.

I liked this a lot! I swapped out the cream cheese for plain greek yogurt and omitted the breadcrumbs to make this healthier for a diabetic. For the stuffing mixture, I added kale and broccoli florets. I also increased the amount of garlic I used. I added in some thyme and basil. and coriander leaves Moving forward, I would drain the bacon grease and add less butter, as my veggies swam in the mixture. I would also season the mushrooms a bit and add in the onion. I would possibly switch the bacon for well marinated pork or chicken. I look forward to making these again. Also didn't feel like brining my blender out, so I mixed it by hand. I loved the texture.

Great recipe. I omitted the bacon for a vegetarian version, toasted focaccia for the bread crumbs and absolutely did not blend it all together. I turned off the heat of the skillet when the onion/mushrooms mixture was ready, added the bread, the cream cheese and the blue cheese so they melted a little and scooped them onto the mushroom caps. I also stuffed a couple of gourmet tomatoes previously seeded, drizzled it all with truffle oil and it was DELICIOUS! Overall a winner recipe and one I'll do it dozens of times.
Blue Bacon Stuffed Mushrooms by Maggie Lopez. Subbed jalapenos; bacon on top; mixed in bowl, not blender.

10.27.14 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/137428/blue-bacon-stuffed-mushrooms/ ... Yeah, I subbed jalapenos for the mushrooms. Lighten up, it's okayyyy! :D I think my review is still valid. I would've liked the bacon to stay crispy so I'd put it on top next time. Oh, I didn't blend it - just mixed in a bowl. Other than that, no suggestions - just if you're using jalapenos, watch out for leaving too many seeds. I had a little sweat going. Really, I did! :D

Yum. I followed recipe except for the following adjustments:
- a little less blue cheese because mine was a very strong blue cheese
-mixed with my hands rather than blender
- substituted sun-dried tomatoes for onions and sautéed for only five minutes
It was really savory and the consistency was perfect tot our taste. Great recipe, thanks.

SOOOO GOOD! I followed Sunnybyrd's review and just mixed everything together in a bowl w/o using the blender to have more texture and b/c, frankly, I didn't feel like getting the blender dirty, lol, but I'm glad I decided not to blend it, b/c the different textures were wonderful! I will def be making these over and over~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)
used bacon crumble and was delicious
Made as printed. Delicious!
These were to die for! Delicious! My husband has asked for them a few times since and they come out perfect every time!

YUM! Only made small changes. I used vegetarian bacon and used cheddar cheese instead of blue cheese (not a blue cheese fan). The cheddar got lost, but I can see where feta might be a good substitution.
Absolutely the best appetizer I have done. I need to get it a little more crumbly in the mix cause it felt a little pasty.

Best ever, everyone loved it. Followed the directions exactly, which is what I always do when making something for the first time. If I want to tweek it later, I will. This one doesn’t need a tweek at all. Thanks for sharing
Delicious and easy to make.
No changes to the recipe aside from using buttermilk blue cheese. They came out very rich, and very good.
If you don't have one of these tasty little apps in your mouth right now and two more in your hand, you're not living your best life. Just drop everything and go make these!
